planting.note: Plant container-grown divisions in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade in spring or early fall; a few hours of gentle morning sun deepens the leaf veining without scorching it.

directions: Plant divisions in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Cracked Ice is a Terra Nova Nurseries foamy bells hybrid prized for large, deeply lobed leaves in cool blue-green tones overlaid with dramatic silvery-pink veining that intensifies in the cool temperatures of early spring and fall. Small white flowers rise on wiry stems above the foliage in late spring, but the mottled, marbled leaf display is the main event through the whole growing season. It forms a tight, non-stoloniferous clump rather than spreading by runners, so it stays where it is planted and pairs well at the front of a shaded border with hostas and ferns. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to maintain vigor.

planting.note: Plant container-grown divisions in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade in spring or early fall; the trailing stems make it especially well suited to hanging baskets, mixed containers, or the top of a shaded retaining wall.

directions: Plant divisions in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Sunrise Falls was bred by Terra Nova Nurseries as one of the first trailing heucherellas, sending out long, lax stems that cascade over a container edge or spread as an unusually vigorous groundcover rather than forming a tight clump. The large, maple-shaped leaves emerge bright yellow-gold with contrasting red veins and take on deeper red tints as nights cool in fall. Small cream flowers appear on short spikes in late spring but are secondary to the trailing foliage display. Give it a spot with a little morning sun to keep the gold color vivid, and consistent moisture, since trailing stems dry out faster than a compact clump.

planting.note: Plant container-grown divisions in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade in spring or early fall; deadhead spent flower scapes to tidy the clump once the early-summer bloom flush fades.

directions: Plant divisions in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Pink Fizz is a Terra Nova Nurseries foamy bells selection grown as much for its flowers as its foliage. Large, deeply lobed, soft green leaves carry a light silvery overlay and heavy wine-red to purple veining, and from early through midsummer hot-pink buds open to clear pink, bell-shaped flowers held well above the foliage on airy scapes. It forms a full, well-behaved clump rather than spreading by runners, making it a reliable edger for a shaded path or the front of a woodland border. Keep soil consistently moist through summer, and divide congested clumps in spring every three to four years.

planting.note: Plant container divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich, slightly acidic, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Sterling Silver will not come true from seed and must be propagated by division or tissue culture.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, slightly acidic, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Sterling Silver is a Terra Nova Nurseries introduction bred as an improvement on the older silver-leaf brunnera cultivars, with larger, wider leaves that carry an almost entirely silver overlay broken only by narrow green veins and a thin green margin. The bold, textured foliage holds up better in heat and humidity than many silver brunneras, resisting the summer scorch that can disfigure older selections. In early spring, loose sprays of small, sky-blue, forget-me-not flowers rise above the emerging leaves before the foliage reaches full size. Provide consistent moisture and afternoon shade in warmer zones to keep the silver leaves pristine through summer.

planting.note: Plant container divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich, slightly acidic, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Silver Charm will not come true from seed and must be propagated by division or tissue culture.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, slightly acidic, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Silver Charm is a Terra Nova Nurseries brunnera with heart-shaped leaves that carry a dense, reflective silver overlay set off by contrasting emerald-green veins and a narrow green edge. The dense, mounding foliage clump holds its good looks from spring through most of the growing season, remaining attractive well after the flower display has finished. In early spring, sprays of small, pale sky-blue flowers rise on wiry stems above the developing leaves, echoing true forget-me-nots. Keep the soil consistently moist and provide afternoon shade in the warmer part of its range, since silver-leaf brunneras scorch quickly if allowed to dry out in direct sun.

planting.note: Divide established clumps immediately after flowering or in early fall in moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade; Benediction is noted for good resistance to the powdery mildew that disfigures many lungworts in humid summers.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Benediction is an American selection of Pulmonaria angustifolia grown for flowers of an unusually dark, saturated cobalt blue that opens in early spring on stalks just above the foliage, without the pink-to-blue color shift typical of most lungworts. The lush, deep green, unspotted-to-lightly-spotted leaves are wider spaced with silver markings than many green-leaved lungworts and stay clean and mildew-free through summer better than most cultivars, making it a strong choice for humid climates. It spreads slowly into a dense, weed-suppressing clump well suited to mass planting under deciduous trees. Keep soil consistently moist and divide congested clumps after flowering to maintain vigor.

planting.note: Divide established clumps in early spring before flowering or immediately after bloom, replanting promptly into moisture-retentive, humus-rich soil in shade; it performs best in cool-summer climates and resents prolonged heat and dryness.

directions: Grow in humus-rich, moisture-retentive soil in full to partial shade; David Ward is a variegated sport of red lungwort found at Beth Chatto's nursery in England and named for her propagator. Unlike most lungworts, its soft, semi-evergreen leaves are unspotted and instead edged in a creamy white margin around pale green centers, giving the clump a bright, luminous quality even before flowering begins. Coral-red, funnel-shaped flowers open in late winter and early spring, among the earliest lungwort blooms of the season and a valuable nectar source for early-emerging pollinators. It is somewhat fussier than the species and can be slow to establish, so give it a permanently moist, well-drained site and protection from hot afternoon sun and summer drought.

planting.note: Divide clumps in early spring before new growth begins or in fall, or plant container-grown specimens in well-drained, slightly acidic, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Divide clumps in early spring or fall, or plant container specimens in well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade; Freya is a compact, clump-forming longspur barrenwort selected for its lilac-purple, spidery flowers, each petal spur tipped in contrasting white along with a matching white-centered sepal, held on wiry stems just above the emerging foliage in mid-spring. The heart-shaped leaflets open with a bronze-red flush before settling into a fresh green, and the evergreen-to-semi-evergreen foliage provides low, weed-suppressing groundcover through the seasons. Like the species, it tolerates the dry, root-filled shade beneath established deciduous trees far better than most shade perennials once established. Cut back tattered old foliage to the ground in late winter before the new flowers and leaves emerge, to keep the delicate spring bloom display visible.

planting.note: Plant divisions in fall in moist to moderately dry, slightly acidic to neutral, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade; established clumps should not be disturbed unnecessarily, since flowering improves markedly with age.

directions: Plant divisions in moist to moderately dry, slightly acidic soil in partial to full shade; Domino is a 2004 Darrell Probst introduction and RHS Award of Garden Merit winner prized for its exceptionally prolific spring flower display, with a single well-established clump capable of producing over a hundred blooms. Each flower pairs long, white-spurred petals with a contrasting purple-maroon cup at the center, giving the sprays of blossoms a crisp bicolor sparkle above the emerging, heart-shaped leaflets. Like other barrenworts, it tolerates the dry shade beneath established trees better than almost any other groundcover once it settles in, spreading gradually into a dense, weed-suppressing colony. Cut old foliage to the ground in late winter before new growth begins so the heavy spring bloom is not obscured by tattered leaves.

planting.note: Divide clumps in early spring before flowering or plant container-grown plants in moist, humus-rich, well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral soil in part to full shade.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in part to full shade; Merlin is a Young's barrenwort selection notable for its unusually dark coloring, with pointed purple buds opening to nodding, spurless flowers in burgundy-violet and white that hover above the foliage on wiry stems in mid to late spring. The broadly oval leaflets emerge bronze-tinged before turning pale green for summer, giving the compact clump multi-season interest beyond the bloom period. It spreads gradually by rhizomes into a refined, small-scale groundcover well suited to the front of a shaded border or tucked among ferns and hellebores. Once established it tolerates the dry, root-filled shade under large deciduous trees notably better than most other shade perennials.
